notes: Parts are the same as before, but pi1 changed type from raspberry-pi-4 to a new type, raspberry-pi-3b.

Why: the raspberry-pi-4 catalogue card has a single GPIO_HEADER port. Both jumper leads therefore landed on the same node, which put the button's two sides on one net and shorted it. The button was wired correctly. The Pi was the problem.

The new type gives each of the 40 header pins its own port, named in physical pin order. The GND pins are one node, and so are the 5V pins and the 3V3 pins. It also has a CSI camera socket port. The board in the diagram has a 40-pin header, full-size HDMI and 3 USB ports, so it looks like a Pi 3-class board rather than a Pi 4. lookup_part found no Pi 3 card, so I defined the type myself.

Wiring follows the circuit image. The black lead goes from GND.1 (physical pin 6, right column, beside GP3) to breadboard hole 3t.a. The orange lead goes from GPIO17 (pin 11) to 5t.a. The tutorial's code uses Button(17) with the internal pull-up, so no external resistor is used.

The button straddles rows 3 and 5. Side 1 (1.l, 1.r) is in row 3, the GND row. Side 2 (2.l, 2.r) is in row 5, the GPIO17 row. Pressing it connects GPIO17 to GND. The exact hole columns (c and e) are my reading of the image.
In the breadboard catalogue naming, the picture's numbered rows are the 'column' number and the lettered a-e columns are the 'row' letter, so 3t.a is row 3, column a.
The ribbon cable type is the Pi 5 camera cable from the lookup. The tutorial's cable is the standard Pi camera ribbon, and the cable is only a joiner.
